head: Nobody saw the oil shock.
Shell had rehearsed it.
slides.sub: How a small London planning team changed what managers were ready for.

image.label: A 1970s London office window overlooking the Thames at dusk
image.brief: 1970년대 런던 사무실 창가, 해 질 녘 템스강이 내려다보임. 책상 위에 서류와 세계 지도. 차분하고 긴장감 있는 영화 톤. 로고 없음.

head: Oil demand rose every year.
So did the forecasts.
body: Through the 1950s and 1960s, oil was cheap and demand kept climbing. Oil companies planned refineries and tankers years ahead.
Their forecasts mostly drew yesterday's line a little further. For a long time, that worked.

image.label: Oil tankers and a refinery under a calm sky
image.brief: 1960년대 정유 공장과 유조선들. 평온한 하늘, 번영의 분위기. 실제 회사 로고와 선박 표식 없음.

head: The planners asked
what producers wanted.
body: At Shell's Group Planning in London, Pierre Wack and Ted Newland studied the oil-producing countries, not just the demand charts.
Some producers already earned more than they could spend. Why pump ever more oil, when it might be worth more left in the ground?

image.label: Silhouettes of two men studying maps and charts
image.brief: 지도와 그래프를 들여다보는 두 남성의 실루엣. 1970년대 사무실, 담배 연기, 노란 조명. 얼굴은 보이지 않게.

head: The first warnings
changed nothing.
body: The team wrote several possible futures, including one where supply was tight and prices jumped.
Wack later wrote that managers read them, nodded, and kept planning as before. A new possibility on paper did not change how they saw the business.

image.label: A report left closed on a boardroom table
image.brief: 회의실 탁자 위에 덮인 채 놓인 보고서. 사람들은 떠나고 빈 의자만 남은 장면.

head: Managers ignore the warning.
What do you do?
body: You run the planning team. Your best analysis says the old world may end, but leaders still trust the familiar forecast.

options.text: Rewrite the scenarios to show what each manager would have to do if prices jumped
options.feedback: It takes far more work and means challenging senior people's view of their own business. Keep swiping.

options.text: Build a sharper single forecast with the price rise as the official prediction
options.feedback: One bold forecast is easy to act on, but if the timing is wrong, you lose all credibility. Keep swiping.

options.text: Stop pushing and plan to react quickly if a crisis comes
options.feedback: It keeps the peace now, but a giant company may be too slow to turn once the crisis starts. Keep swiping.

image.label: Three paths splitting on a foggy road
image.brief: 안개 낀 길이 세 갈래로 갈라지는 장면. 1970년대 유럽 시골 풍경.

head: They stopped predicting.
They made it feel real.
body: Wack's team reworked the scenarios to walk managers through the consequences: what a sudden price rise would mean for refineries, tankers and markets.
The goal was not to be right about the future. It was to change the picture in managers' heads.

image.label: A planner presenting branching charts to a room of silhouettes
image.brief: 갈래가 나뉘는 도표를 앞에 두고 발표하는 사람과 그것을 듣는 실루엣들. 1970년대 회의실, 슬라이드 프로젝터 빛.

head: October 1973.
The future arrived.
body: War broke out in the Middle East. Arab oil producers cut supply and imposed an embargo on some Western countries.
Queues formed at petrol stations. The old world of cheap, endless oil was gone almost overnight.

image.label: A long line of 1970s cars at a petrol station
image.brief: 1970년대 주유소 앞에 길게 늘어선 자동차 행렬. '품절' 표지판. 실제 브랜드 표식 없음.

slides.label: rise in posted crude oil prices between October 1973 and early 1974
body: Rivals had to rethink everything at once. At Shell, managers had already imagined this world and some of the moves it would demand.

image.label: An oil price chart shooting sharply upward
image.brief: 급격히 치솟는 유가 그래프. 어두운 배경에 붉은 선.

head: Not a forecast.
A head start.
body: Wack later wrote that Shell's managers adjusted faster than many rivals, because the shock fit a story they had already thought through.
Scenario planning became part of how Shell plans, a story often told in business schools ever since.

image.label: A calm control room while the outside world is in turmoil
image.brief: 바깥은 혼란스럽지만 차분하게 움직이는 1970년대 사무실. 창밖에 불안한 하늘.

head: Forecasts guess the future.
Scenarios prepare minds.
body: Most planning assumes tomorrow looks like today, and people resist evidence that it won't. Shell's planners attacked that habit directly.
By making managers live through several futures, they changed their mental map before reality forced it.

image.label: Several transparent maps layered over each other
image.brief: 서로 겹쳐진 반투명 지도 여러 장. 각기 다른 길이 표시된 그래픽.

head: Don't bet on one future.
Rehearse several.
body: Warnings rarely change behavior. Walking through what you would actually do often does.
**Try it today:** write two short stories of next year, one where your biggest cost doubles and one where demand halves. What would you do first in each?

image.label: A single lamp lighting a desk with several open notebooks
image.brief: 램프 하나가 비추는 책상 위에 펼쳐진 노트 여러 권. 조용하고 사색적인 분위기.

factChecks.note: Pierre Wack과 Ted Newland가 런던의 Royal Dutch/Shell Group Planning에서 1970년대 초 시나리오 작업을 이끌었다는 내용은 Wack의 1985년 HBR 논문 두 편과 Shell 공식 자료로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] Pierre Wack의 Shell Group Planning 시나리오 작업과 OPEC 주도 위기 시나리오 확인.
첫 시나리오(1972년 무렵)가 경영진의 행동을 바꾸지 못했고, 이후 시나리오가 각 시나리오에서 경영진이 해야 할 일을 보여주는 방식으로 바뀌었다는 설명은 Wack의 HBR 논문("Scenarios: Uncharted Waters Ahead", 1985) 기준입니다. 정확한 연도는 원문으로 확인하세요.
산유국이 수입을 다 쓸 수 없어 생산을 늘릴 동기가 약했다는 분석은 Wack의 논문에 나오는 논리를 풀어 쓴 것입니다. 직접 인용은 하지 않았습니다.
"about 4x": 1973년 10월 욤키푸르 전쟁과 아랍 산유국 금수 조치 이후 원유 공시가격이 1974년 초까지 배럴당 약 3달러에서 약 11~12달러로 오른 것은 널리 기록된 사실입니다. EIA 등 자료로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1973~74년 유가 약 2.5~3달러에서 약 11달러로 상승(약 4배) 확인.
Shell이 경쟁사보다 빨리 대응했다는 평가는 주로 Wack 본인과 Shell 측 서술에 근거합니다. 카드에서 "Wack later wrote", "a story often told"로 표시했습니다. Shell이 메이저 중 약체에서 최상위권으로 올라섰다는 흔한 이야기는 순위가 자료마다 달라 카드에 넣지 않았습니다.
시나리오가 석유 위기를 '예측'했다는 식의 과장은 피했습니다. 시나리오는 예측이 아니라 대비였고, 위기의 시점·촉발 사건(전쟁)은 예견하지 못했다는 점을 확인하세요.
